taxonomy.note: Current Kew/POWO accepts Symphyotrichum praealtum and includes Texas in the native range.

target_zone_range.evidence_basis: Travis — University of Texas Plant Resources Center Travis County herbarium specimen index includes Symphyotrichum praealtum. A historical Berlandier specimen from a route between Bexar and the upper Guadalupe is not assigned to a modern county and is not counted.
target_zone_range.blocking_issue: Need two additional exact target-zone native counties under the modern species concept.
target_zone_range.guardrail: Do not convert broad Texas nativity, a historical travel route, or horticultural records into exact county evidence.

morphology.look_here_first: Look for a tall rhizomatous colony with narrow lance-shaped leaves and a broad pyramidal many-headed inflorescence. Larger stems may be reddish with longitudinal lines of hairs; confirm stem/leaf attachment and phyllaries before separating it from other tall white-to-purple asters.
morphology.key_separation: S. praealtum is typically taller and more strongly willow-leaved/pyramidal than low bushy aromatic S. oblongifolium. Keep S. lanceolatum in the comparison because both can be tall, rhizomatous, moist-site asters.
